info.description:
## PermitStack Building Permit API

Access 121M+ building permits across 8,000+ U.S. cities in 48 states and DC (905 active data sources including counties and statewide feeds, plus 75 historical archives), drawn from official city and county permit systems and open-data portals and re-ingested nightly for most sources.

### Getting started
1. Sign up at [permit-stack.com](https://permit-stack.com/#pricing) for a free API key (100 req/day)
2. Pass your key as `X-API-Key` header on every request
3. See the `/v1/permits/search` endpoint to get started

### Rate limits
Tier       | Requests/min | Requests/day
-----------|--------------|-------------
Free       | 30           | 100
Indie      | 30           | 1,000
Hobbyist   | 30           | 2,500
Developer  | 60           | 10,000
Business   | 200          | 100,000
Scale      | 500          | 500,000

Free keys cover the last 30 days of permits; every paid tier has full historical access.
Higher volume or custom terms: support@permit-stack.com

### Support
support@permit-stack.com

get.description:
Public stats endpoint — no auth required.
Returns aggregate coverage numbers for marketing/transparency.
Cached server-side for 30 minutes.

Search building permits by location, date, category, contractor and more.

Filters combine with AND. Supply at least one narrowing filter -- a city, ZIP,
jurisdiction, date range or lat/lng radius -- for a query that returns quickly.

Results are paginated and ordered newest-first on the permit's best available date
(`date_issued`, falling back to `date_filed`). `total` is exact up to 10,000; beyond
that it stops counting and returns `total: 10000` with `total_capped: true`, meaning
"10,000 or more". If the count cannot finish in time the response carries
`total: null` with `total_unknown: true` -- an unknown total is reported as unknown
and never as a number. Rows are unaffected either way; page through them normally.

`category=hvac` matches HVAC and MECHANICAL together, because AC and furnace work is
filed under either depending on the city. Unknown parameter names are rejected with a
400 rather than ignored, so a typo can never silently return unfiltered results.

Free-tier keys are limited to a recent window; paid tiers have full history.

Record credits: when there is no active plan entitlement, one credit is charged per returned record, with a one-credit minimum for successful empty data responses. Property responses count their permits. CSV sizing previews cost 0 credits and share the per-key 60/minute request budget. Credit accounts cannot receive owner or contractor contact fields. An empty or expired wallet returns 402 with a pack URL before the data query. Concurrent requests for the same wallet can return 409; retry after one second. A final JSON page may overdraw once; the next purchase first covers that debt. CSV downloads are capped at the remaining credit balance.

get.description:
Incremental data feed (change-data-capture). Page the dataset ordered by
(updated_at, id). Omit `cursor` for the initial full load; persist `next_cursor` and pass
it back after each nightly ingest to receive only new + changed permits. Upsert-only:
permits we delete (duplicate copies removed in cleanups) are listed separately by
GET /v1/permits/sync/deletions, which pages the same way.

**Keeping a mirror exact.** Upsert every record from this feed, and drop every
`permit_id` that GET /v1/permits/sync/deletions returns when called with the SAME
`record_kind`, `state` and `category` you pass here. A permit can leave a filtered
feed without being deleted -- re-classified (roofing -> hvac), re-located to another
state, re-labelled as a non-building record, or its source switched off -- and the
deletions feed then lists it for every filter it no longer matches, and never for one
it still matches. A permit that moves INTO your filter arrives here with a new
`updated_at`. Membership changes are recorded from 2026-10-25; category and state moves
before that date were not, so a mirror built with `category=` or `state=` before then
should re-pull once (or sync unfiltered with `record_kind=all` and filter locally).

get.description:
Permits to drop from a mirror built with /v1/permits/sync.

/v1/permits/sync is upsert-only, so a permit we delete (almost always a duplicate copy of a
permit that still exists under another id) would otherwise live on in a mirror and 404 on
/v1/permits/{id}. Drop every `permit_id` listed here. Same cursor contract as /sync: omit
`cursor` (or pass `since`) to start, then pass back `next_cursor`. When the deleted copy's
permit still exists under another id, `replaced_by` names it. Every delete is recorded by a
database trigger, so this list covers all deletions from 2026-09-24 on, whatever removed them.

**Call it with the same `record_kind`, `state` and `category` as your /v1/permits/sync
calls.** It also lists permits that LEFT that feed without being deleted (`kind =
"left_feed"`, the permit still exists): we stopped serving the source
(`reason = "jurisdiction_deactivated"`), it was re-labelled as a non-building
record (`left_permit_set:<kind>`, or `record_kind_changed:<kind>` for a
record that was not a permit), or -- from 2026-10-25 -- it was re-classified or moved to
another state or source (`category_changed:OLD->NEW`,
`state_changed:OLD->NEW`, `jurisdiction_changed`; for a move,
`jurisdiction_id` is the source it LEFT and `moved_to_jurisdiction_id` the one it joined).
`reason` names the latest change, except that a re-label or a stopped source still in
force keeps its reason through later changes. Each entry is judged against the permit as it is
NOW: one that still matches your filters is never listed for you, and one that comes back
is re-sent by /v1/permits/sync with a new `updated_at`.

A page holds at most `limit` results. To reach them it examines records past ones that do
not concern you (up to 250,000 per page), so after a large
re-classification a page can still hold fewer than `limit` results, even none, while
`has_more` is true. Keep paging until `has_more` is false; `next_cursor` always advances
past everything examined.

get.description:
What CHANGED, instead of re-reading everything: permit transitions
(new_permit, status_change, issued, completed, expired) built from the daily
ingest diff, filterable by city, state, category and jurisdiction.

**This is the endpoint to poll on a schedule, and `cursor` is how to poll it.**
Save the `next_cursor` from each response and pass it back as `cursor` on the
next call; you then receive only what you have not already seen, in the order it
was detected, with no duplicates and no gap. Page until a response comes back
shorter than `per_page`, save that last `next_cursor`, and resume there tomorrow.

**WHERE YOU START MATTERS, AND THE FIRST CALL DOES NOT START AT THE BEGINNING.**
A call with NO cursor returns the NEWEST events and its `next_cursor` is the
frontier -- a watermark at "now". Pass it straight back and you correctly get 0
results, because you have just declared yourself caught up. That is exactly what
a poller wants: from here on you receive everything new. It is NOT a backfill,
and it will not walk history for you -- there are 75,544 events behind that
watermark for the Tampa filter below alone.

To start somewhere else, build the cursor yourself: it is
`<ISO-8601 timestamp>|<event id>`, and `|0` is a valid id floor.

    # start polling from now (typical):
    GET /v1/permits/events?city=Tampa&state=FL&category=roofing
        &event_type=new_permit                       -> save next_cursor
    # ...then, from the next call onward:
    GET ...&cursor=2026-09-08T04%3A09%3A16.381111%2B00%3A00%7C51823904

    # start from a chosen point instead (backfill the last 30 days, then keep polling):
    GET ...&cursor=2026-08-11T00%3A00%3A00%2B00%3A00%7C0

One call answers what a paged re-pull of /v1/permits/search costs hundreds of.
Measured 2026-09-09, that Tampa query returns **38 records in a single call**;
the same question asked by re-pulling search pages 1-100 twelve times a day
costs ~9,600 requests and runs into the daily cap.

`detected_after` still works and is fine for an ad-hoc look at a window, but it
is the wrong tool for a poller: it is INCLUSIVE, and one ingest batch stamps
thousands of events with a single identical `detected_at` (measured 2026-09-10:
3,688 timestamps carry over 1,000 events each, the largest 1,370,561). A poller
that stores the newest `detected_at` and passes it back therefore re-receives
that whole batch every time. `cursor` breaks the tie on the event id and does not.

Supplying a `cursor` returns events oldest-unseen first, which is what lets a
batch be paged safely; without one you get the newest first, for browsing.
`cursor` and `page` are alternatives -- passing both is a 400 rather than a
silently skipped page.

Ingest runs once a day, so a daily poll is enough; `detected_at` is when WE saw
the change, not when the city recorded it. For push instead of poll, register a
webhook (developer tier and above) and skip the polling entirely.

Record credits: when there is no active plan entitlement, one credit is charged per returned record, with a one-credit minimum for successful empty data responses. Property responses count their permits. CSV sizing previews cost 0 credits and share the per-key 60/minute request budget. Credit accounts cannot receive owner or contractor contact fields. An empty or expired wallet returns 402 with a pack URL before the data query. Concurrent requests for the same wallet can return 409; retry after one second. A final JSON page may overdraw once; the next purchase first covers that debt. CSV downloads are capped at the remaining credit balance.

JurisdictionCoverage.description:

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable PermitStack id. Pass to GET /v1/permits/{id}.

permit_number.title: Permit Number
permit_number.description: The permit number as the issuing jurisdiction publishes it. Not unique across jurisdictions, and not always present.

status.title: Status
status.description: One of FILED, ISSUED, IN_PROGRESS, FINAL, EXPIRED, CANCELLED, REVOKED, INTERCONNECTED, UNKNOWN -- normalised by us from each source's own vocabulary. UNKNOWN means no recognized normalized status is available; the source value may be missing or unrecognized. It does not establish whether the permit is active. INTERCONNECTED comes from the California NEM solar feed.

category.title: Category
category.description: Trade/work classification, UPPERCASE. One of: NEW_CONSTRUCTION, RENOVATION, DEMOLITION, ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, MECHANICAL, ROOFING, SOLAR, BATTERY, EV_CHARGER, HVAC, FIRE_ALARM, SIGN, FENCE, POOL, FOUNDATION, ADDITION, INTERIOR_REMODEL, GRADING, OTHER. Derived by us from the permit type and description, not published by the city. NOTE when FILTERING: ?category=hvac matches HVAC *and* MECHANICAL, and ?category=mechanical does the same, because HVAC work is routinely filed as MECHANICAL -- they are one market and a bare equality would hide half of it.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Free-form keywords extracted from the description (e.g. 'pool', 'reroof'). Additive; do not rely on a fixed vocabulary.

property_type.title: Property Type
property_type.description: RESIDENTIAL, COMMERCIAL, INDUSTRIAL, MIXED_USE or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN means no recognized normalized property type is available. Source omissions, mapping gaps or unrecognized values can cause this.

address_street.title: Address Street
address_street.description: Held street address mapped from source fields. It may be assembled from components or split from a postal address; spacing can vary. Address matching normalises whitespace.

address_city.title: Address City
address_city.description: City recorded for this held permit. Null means no usable normalized city is available; it does not establish that the property is outside a city or that the source never publishes one.

address_state.title: Address State
address_state.description: 2-letter state recorded for this held permit. Null means no usable normalized state is available. A state search can still include such rows using independent jurisdiction evidence.

parcel_id.title: Parcel Id
parcel_id.description: Assessor parcel number / APN, either published with the permit or matched from an appraiser roll by situs address. Formatting varies by source and is preserved. Null means no usable parcel is mapped on this record; it does not establish that the upstream feed or property has no parcel. Filterable via ?parcel= after the parcel index is refreshed.

description_raw.title: Description Raw
description_raw.description: Held source-derived work description. Text may be combined from multiple fields, cleaned, or have contacts removed. Whole-value placeholders may become null. Used by the category classifier; not a verbatim copy or evidence that work was completed.
examples: RE-ROOF: remove existing shingles, install 39 sq architectural shingles

estimated_value.title: Estimated Value
estimated_value.description: Declared job value in USD, as published. Frequently null and occasionally nominal -- treat 0 and 1 as 'not stated'.

date_filed.title: Date Filed
date_filed.description: Application/filing date where mapped and usable. Null means no usable held filing date is available; source omissions, mapping gaps or validation can cause this.

date_issued.title: Date Issued
date_issued.description: Issue date where mapped and usable. Null means no usable held issue date is available; it does not establish what dates the source publishes. date_after/date_before filter on COALESCE(date_issued, date_filed); issued_after uses only date_issued.

date_completed.title: Date Completed
date_completed.description: Completion/final date where the source publishes one. Usually null.

approval_days.title: Approval Days
approval_days.description: Calendar days from date_filed to date_issued (null unless both dates present)

construction_days.title: Construction Days
construction_days.description: Calendar days from date_issued to date_completed (null unless both dates present)

contractor_name.title: Contractor Name
contractor_name.description: Contractor name linked to the held permit record after cleaning and matching. Null values can reflect source omissions, mapping gaps or unmatched names. The jurisdiction_coverage block reports contractor-name presence on the current page; it does not prove complete source capture.

contractor_id.title: Contractor Id
contractor_id.description: Opaque id of the contractor linked to this held permit. Use GET /v1/contractors/{id} for its record. Null means no contractor is linked; source omissions and matching gaps can both cause this.

owner_name.title: Owner Name
owner_name.description: Owner name recorded by the source, subject to field access. A present owner name and absent contractor name do not establish who filed the permit, a homeowner, purchase intent or a sales opportunity. Source omissions and matching gaps can explain missing contractor data. Review the owner_filed filter semantics and source coverage.

owner_address.title: Owner Address
owner_address.description: Property-owner mailing address. Business plan ($149/mo) and above; null below that access gate. Joined from held county assessor records by parcel. Source availability, capture and matching vary by jurisdiction; loading a roll does not establish complete address coverage. A null value does not establish that a property has no owner on record.

jurisdiction_name.title: Jurisdiction Name
jurisdiction_name.description: The PermitStack data source this permit came from -- a city, county or statewide feed, which is not always the permit's own city.

latitude.title: Latitude
latitude.description: WGS84 latitude. Null means no usable latitude is held after mapping and any geocoding; it does not establish that the source lacks coordinates. Permits without usable coordinates are absent from radius, bbox and polygon search.

location_source.title: Location Source
location_source.description: Where the coordinates came from. 'source' = published by the city with the permit record, as good as the city's own data. 'geocoded' = derived by us from the site address (TIGER, address-centroid quality), which for a structure set back from the road, such as an antenna mast, marks the property address rather than the structure. 'derived' = set by us by another method (typically a parcel-centroid join), so treat it as ours, not the city's. 'source' is judged per feed: in a feed that publishes coordinates, a minority of rows whose record lacked them may have been filled by our geocoder before 2026-09-21, when it began logging successes, and those read 'source'. Null when latitude/longitude are null.

enrichment.description: Structured detail parsed from the description (e.g. solar kW) where we could extract it. Null for most permits.

record_kind.title: Record Kind
record_kind.description: permit | contractor | tag | non_building | admin. Some portals mix non-permit records (contractor registrations, right-of-way, administrative) into the same feed; we store them and label them rather than counting them as permits. Search and export return record_kind='permit' only unless you ask otherwise.

date_expired.title: Date Expired
date_expired.description: Expiry date where published. Deliberately NOT null-checked against the future the way the other dates are -- an expiry legitimately lies ahead.

fee_amount.title: Fee Amount
fee_amount.description: Permit/inspection fee where mapped and usable. A null value does not establish that the source never publishes fees or that no fee was charged.

square_footage.title: Square Footage
square_footage.description: Project square footage, where published. Usually null.

applicant_name.title: Applicant Name
applicant_name.description: Whoever filed the application. On most feeds this is the OWNER; on a few it is the contractor, and for those tenants we map it to contractor_name instead. Never assume which one it is from this field alone.

contractor_license.title: Contractor License
contractor_license.description: Contractor's licence number as published or as matched against a state licence-board roster. A free public identifier; contact details remain gated to /v1/contractors/{id} on Developer+.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When PermitStack first ingested this record (ISO 8601). NOT a date the city published -- use date_filed/date_issued for that.

PermitDetail.title: PermitDetail
PermitDetail.description:
PermitSummary plus the nine columns that only a single-permit lookup used to carry.
Also returned inline by search and sync with ?fields=full (Developer and above).

PermitEnrichment.title: PermitEnrichment
PermitEnrichment.description:
Curated subset of the offline LLM enrichment (permits.enriched_data).

Present only on the ~1-2% of permits that have been enriched so far
(prioritized toward SOLAR/ROOFING/NEW_CONSTRUCTION). null otherwise.

contractor_id.title: Contractor Id
contractor_id.description: Stable id of the contractor of record, joinable to /v1/contractors/{id}. Null means no contractor is linked to this held row; source omissions, mapping gaps or unmatched names can cause this.

property_type.title: Property Type
property_type.description: RESIDENTIAL, COMMERCIAL, MIXED_USE, ... or UNKNOWN, as on /v1/permits/search.

description.title: Description
description.description: The permit's scope of work as the jurisdiction published it (description_raw on search).

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to receive only events you have not seen yet, with no duplicates and no gap. Null when this page cannot define a resume point (i.e. a `page` beyond the first, where the newest row on the page is not the newest overall).

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable PermitStack id. Pass to GET /v1/permits/{id}.

permit_number.title: Permit Number
permit_number.description: The permit number as the issuing jurisdiction publishes it. Not unique across jurisdictions, and not always present.

status.title: Status
status.description: One of FILED, ISSUED, IN_PROGRESS, FINAL, EXPIRED, CANCELLED, REVOKED, INTERCONNECTED, UNKNOWN -- normalised by us from each source's own vocabulary. UNKNOWN means no recognized normalized status is available; the source value may be missing or unrecognized. It does not establish whether the permit is active. INTERCONNECTED comes from the California NEM solar feed.

category.title: Category
category.description: Trade/work classification, UPPERCASE. One of: NEW_CONSTRUCTION, RENOVATION, DEMOLITION, ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, MECHANICAL, ROOFING, SOLAR, BATTERY, EV_CHARGER, HVAC, FIRE_ALARM, SIGN, FENCE, POOL, FOUNDATION, ADDITION, INTERIOR_REMODEL, GRADING, OTHER. Derived by us from the permit type and description, not published by the city. NOTE when FILTERING: ?category=hvac matches HVAC *and* MECHANICAL, and ?category=mechanical does the same, because HVAC work is routinely filed as MECHANICAL -- they are one market and a bare equality would hide half of it.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Free-form keywords extracted from the description (e.g. 'pool', 'reroof'). Additive; do not rely on a fixed vocabulary.

property_type.title: Property Type
property_type.description: RESIDENTIAL, COMMERCIAL, INDUSTRIAL, MIXED_USE or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN means no recognized normalized property type is available. Source omissions, mapping gaps or unrecognized values can cause this.

address_street.title: Address Street
address_street.description: Held street address mapped from source fields. It may be assembled from components or split from a postal address; spacing can vary. Address matching normalises whitespace.

address_city.title: Address City
address_city.description: City recorded for this held permit. Null means no usable normalized city is available; it does not establish that the property is outside a city or that the source never publishes one.

address_state.title: Address State
address_state.description: 2-letter state recorded for this held permit. Null means no usable normalized state is available. A state search can still include such rows using independent jurisdiction evidence.

parcel_id.title: Parcel Id
parcel_id.description: Assessor parcel number / APN, either published with the permit or matched from an appraiser roll by situs address. Formatting varies by source and is preserved. Null means no usable parcel is mapped on this record; it does not establish that the upstream feed or property has no parcel. Filterable via ?parcel= after the parcel index is refreshed.

description_raw.title: Description Raw
description_raw.description: Held source-derived work description. Text may be combined from multiple fields, cleaned, or have contacts removed. Whole-value placeholders may become null. Used by the category classifier; not a verbatim copy or evidence that work was completed.
examples: RE-ROOF: remove existing shingles, install 39 sq architectural shingles

estimated_value.title: Estimated Value
estimated_value.description: Declared job value in USD, as published. Frequently null and occasionally nominal -- treat 0 and 1 as 'not stated'.

date_filed.title: Date Filed
date_filed.description: Application/filing date where mapped and usable. Null means no usable held filing date is available; source omissions, mapping gaps or validation can cause this.

date_issued.title: Date Issued
date_issued.description: Issue date where mapped and usable. Null means no usable held issue date is available; it does not establish what dates the source publishes. date_after/date_before filter on COALESCE(date_issued, date_filed); issued_after uses only date_issued.

date_completed.title: Date Completed
date_completed.description: Completion/final date where the source publishes one. Usually null.

approval_days.title: Approval Days
approval_days.description: Calendar days from date_filed to date_issued (null unless both dates present)

construction_days.title: Construction Days
construction_days.description: Calendar days from date_issued to date_completed (null unless both dates present)

contractor_name.title: Contractor Name
contractor_name.description: Contractor name linked to the held permit record after cleaning and matching. Null values can reflect source omissions, mapping gaps or unmatched names. The jurisdiction_coverage block reports contractor-name presence on the current page; it does not prove complete source capture.

contractor_id.title: Contractor Id
contractor_id.description: Opaque id of the contractor linked to this held permit. Use GET /v1/contractors/{id} for its record. Null means no contractor is linked; source omissions and matching gaps can both cause this.

owner_name.title: Owner Name
owner_name.description: Owner name recorded by the source, subject to field access. A present owner name and absent contractor name do not establish who filed the permit, a homeowner, purchase intent or a sales opportunity. Source omissions and matching gaps can explain missing contractor data. Review the owner_filed filter semantics and source coverage.

owner_address.title: Owner Address
owner_address.description: Property-owner mailing address. Business plan ($149/mo) and above; null below that access gate. Joined from held county assessor records by parcel. Source availability, capture and matching vary by jurisdiction; loading a roll does not establish complete address coverage. A null value does not establish that a property has no owner on record.

jurisdiction_name.title: Jurisdiction Name
jurisdiction_name.description: The PermitStack data source this permit came from -- a city, county or statewide feed, which is not always the permit's own city.

latitude.title: Latitude
latitude.description: WGS84 latitude. Null means no usable latitude is held after mapping and any geocoding; it does not establish that the source lacks coordinates. Permits without usable coordinates are absent from radius, bbox and polygon search.

location_source.title: Location Source
location_source.description: Where the coordinates came from. 'source' = published by the city with the permit record, as good as the city's own data. 'geocoded' = derived by us from the site address (TIGER, address-centroid quality), which for a structure set back from the road, such as an antenna mast, marks the property address rather than the structure. 'derived' = set by us by another method (typically a parcel-centroid join), so treat it as ours, not the city's. 'source' is judged per feed: in a feed that publishes coordinates, a minority of rows whose record lacked them may have been filled by our geocoder before 2026-09-21, when it began logging successes, and those read 'source'. Null when latitude/longitude are null.

enrichment.description: Structured detail parsed from the description (e.g. solar kW) where we could extract it. Null for most permits.

PropertySignals.title: PropertySignals
PropertySignals.description:
Boolean/scalar rollups useful for underwriting, valuation and diligence.

Derived from category, tags and enrichment on held matches within the plan's
history window. Dates prefer issue, then filing, then completion date where
available (ISO yyyy-mm-dd). They are permit-date proxies, not verified
installation dates or current equipment condition. Missing records and
classification errors can affect these signals.

TwinRecord.title: TwinRecord
TwinRecord.description:
Another source's copy of the same record (a twin), with its own status and money: the
hearing outcome of a building violation lives on its hearing-feed twin (D4).

contractor_name.title: Contractor Name
contractor_name.description: Fire only for permits pulled by contractors whose name contains this text (case-insensitive) — track a competitor or partner as their new permits arrive.

tags.name: Contractors
tags.description: Search contractors and see their permit history

tags.name: Property History
tags.description: Get permit history for a specific address

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Webhooks attempt signed delivery of eligible matching records after ingestion. Most sources have scheduled nightly ingestion; the dispatcher is scheduled every 60 seconds. That cadence is not an arrival deadline. Source publication, matching windows, backlog, retries and endpoint availability affect delivery. Developer plan ($79/mo) and above.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Pre-aggregated permit counts and valuation from a nightly rollup. Use these instead of paging through search results to count them: they answer 'how many' and 'is it trending' in one millisecond-scale call. Developer plan and above.

tags.name: Credits
tags.description: Prepaid record credit packs: list the packs and check an account's balance. Packs are bought on the dashboard; without a plan covering the call, one credit is charged per returned record.

tags.name: Licensing
tags.description: Contractor licence records as public state licence boards publish them: licence number, type, class, status and dates. Look one up by number and state, or list the licences linked to a contractor. Contractor licensing add-on, $19/mo on Developer; included in Business and Scale. Bond, liability insurance, workers' comp and discipline fields need Contractor licensing Pro (only some boards publish them): Contractor licensing Pro add-on, $29/mo on Developer or Business; included in Scale. No phone, email or street address is returned here.

tags.name: Certificates of Occupancy
tags.description: Certificates of occupancy as cities, counties and state agencies publish them: certificate number, type, status and date, address, parcel, occupancy class, units and the linked permit where we hold it. /v1/certificates/coverage works with any API key, so you can check a place before buying. Certificates of occupancy add-on, $29/mo on Developer; included in Business and Scale.

tags.name: Inspections
tags.description: Building inspections as cities and counties publish them: inspection type, result (pass, fail, partial, cancelled, scheduled), dates and inspector, linked to the permit we hold where the permit number matches. /v1/inspections/coverage works with any API key, so you can check a place before buying. Inspector comments are not included. Building inspections add-on, $19/mo on Developer or Business; included in Scale.

tags.name: Code Violations
tags.description: Code-enforcement violations as cities and counties publish them: case number, violation type and code, category, status, opened and closed dates and, where the source publishes them, fines. Complaints are a separate record kind and are never counted as violations. /v1/violations/coverage works with any API key, so you can check a place before buying; it says which sources keep full history and which keep only a recent window. No owner, complainant or inspector names are included. Code violations add-on, $19/mo on Developer; included in Business and Scale.

tags.name: Development Pipeline
tags.description: Planning and zoning cases (rezonings, site plans, plats and subdivisions, variances, conditional and special uses, annexations, planned developments, comprehensive-plan amendments, demolition and historic reviews) with status, hearing and decision dates, address and parcel, plus council, planning-commission and zoning-board decisions with the outcome and roll-call votes, linked to the case and to the permits that followed where we can match them. Each case carries a generated scope summary (type, zoning change, units, acres, square feet, uses); no applicant, owner or other free text from the source is included. /v1/pipeline/coverage works with any API key, so you can check a place before buying. Development pipeline add-on, $29/mo on Developer; included in Business and Scale.
